subject: RFI: model catalog & licensing details
messages:
From: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@enterprisebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@enterprisebank.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: model catalog & licensing details

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As discussed, Procurement and Legal have a standard RFI focused on model provenance, licensing, and version governance for any inference vendor we evaluate. Can you please provide detailed responses to the attached questionnaire (see "EB-RFI-Model-Questions.pdf") and include:

- A machine-readable export or CSV of your model catalog (models, upstream license, quantization variants, recommended usage)
- Your opinion on compatibility with permissive vs reciprocal open-source licenses and any restrictions you impose
- How you record model provenance, artifacts, and checksum/auditability for onboarded weights
- Your recommended policy for version pinning and how you notify/release updates and security patches

Target: procurement review next Tuesday (2026-05-18). If possible, provide anything redacted for internal notes and a follow-up call to review.

Thanks,
Tom Wallace
Senior Procurement Manager
Enterprise Bank
[Attachment: EB-RFI-Model-Questions.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@enterprisebank.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog & licensing details

Tom —

Appreciate the detailed list. Attached are our responses and supporting artifacts. Summary highlights below, full answers are in the PDF/CSV set attached: redwood-model-catalog.csv, license-compatibility-matrix.pdf, provenance-guidance.md, version-pinning-policy.pdf.

Key points (high-level):
- Model catalog: We maintain a single source-of-truth CSV export (attached) listing every model we serve, the upstream checkpoint and author, license declared by the original model, quantization and variant IDs, and recommended workload profiles. We refresh this export nightly and publish a hashed snapshot for audit (see provenance doc).
- Licensing: We surface the upstream license and provide a compatibility matrix that maps common enterprise policies to risk profiles (permissive = green, reciprocal/viral = yellow/red depending on embedding/derivative use). Redwood does not relicense upstream models; we provide guidance and optional remediation (isolation, proprietary fine-tune wrappers) where licenses restrict commercial use.
- Provenance & auditability: For each onboarded artifact we record source URL, checksum (SHA-256), onboarding date, model lineage (preprocessing, tokenizer version, conversion scripts), and a signed manifest. Manifests are retained for 7 years by default and can be exported for audits.
- Version pinning & updates: Customers can pin to a model version ID at route-level. We publish release notes and datestamped variant hashes; urgent security fixes trigger a high-priority release with backporting guidance. Notifications: audit logs + Console banner + email to configured contacts.

I've attached the full RFI response PDF and the machine-readable catalog CSV. Happy to schedule a 30-min review — are you available Thursday 5/13 afternoon?

Warmly,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-model-catalog.csv, license-compatibility-matrix.pdf, provenance-guidance.md, version-pinning-policy.pdf]

Team —

Looping you both for quick SE/legal input before the 5/13 call. Legal asked:

1) Who signs the manifest (Redwood or customer) and key custody model?
2) Confirm whether our manifests/proofs cover raw upstream checkpoint checksums end-to-end (original source -> converted artifact).
3) Provide 4-5 operational mitigations for reciprocal-license models (e.g., run-in-sidecar, inference-only wrappers, tokenization-only exports, fine-tune locking, read-only data flow).

Tom is available 5/13 2pm ET for a review — I'll host and invite their procurement/legal. Quick answers below would help me prep talking points.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: model catalog & licensing details — Legal follow-up (signing + mitigations)

Marissa / Laura —

Answers below in brief; I'll expand verbally on the call and can attach a short tech note if needed.

1) Signing & key custody: Redwood signs the onboarding manifest using a service key generated in our KMS (customer-facing proofs are our signed manifest plus an optional downloadable manifest signed with a customer-managed key if they enable Dedicated/Private deployment and supply an asymmetric key). KMS keys for Redwood are HSM-backed; customer-managed keys are supported for Private deployments (we do not store customer-supplied private keys).

2) Checksum coverage: Yes — we compute SHA-256 on the original upstream checkpoint (where available) and again after conversion/quantization. Our manifest contains both upstream checksum and serving-artifact checksum along with the conversion script hash, so chain-of-custody is provable. We can provide notarized snapshots (timestamped + signed) for audits.

3) Operational mitigations for reciprocal-licensed models (short bullets for Legal):
- Isolation: Host model in dedicated tenancy (dedicated GPU pool) and restrict artifact export.
- Inference-only API: Disable model weight export and restrict endpoints to token-in/token-out responses; no checkpoint downloads.
- Wrapper licensing: Provide a thin proprietary serving layer (binary or closed-source wrapper) that interacts with model but keeps product code separate.
- Fine-tune control: If customers fine-tune, require training artifacts to be stored in customer-managed buckets with RBAC; Redwood stores only metadata hashes.
- Monitoring & alerts: Detect and block unusual non-API artifact requests; retain logs for audits.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix to hand to Legal tomorrow morning.

—Dev
